_note: Forecast of the next amendment. Bands index BAND in app.js (1 very likely ... 5 very unlikely). Every fact cites an official source: Parliament's bill records (sansad.in), PIB, the Gazette, or the official text and footnotes. Review after each session of Parliament and update asOn. Researched 22 November 2026.
headline: No amendment Bill is close to a final vote. The next amendment is most likely to be about how Lok Sabha seats are shared among the States and when seats reserved for women start. The surest date is 25 January 2030: reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes end then unless Parliament extends them, and it has extended them every time before.

when.why: At the pace of the last ten years, six Acts in ten years, there would be about a 45% chance of at least one Act in any year. The chance is lower now. No Bill is near a final vote, the Government's last attempt failed in April 2026, and the main open question waits for Census 2027, whose counting runs into March 2027.

when.by: By June 2029, when this Lok Sabha's term ends
when.why: Seats reserved for women can start only after constituencies are redrawn on the new census, and the freeze on seat shares ends with the same census. Both make seats a likely subject before the next general election. The April 2026 vote showed there is no agreement yet on how.
Article 334 ends reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes on that date. Parliament has extended the deadline before each of the seven times it fell due.

cands.t: Extending reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes
cands.stage: No Bill yet. Due before 25 January 2030.
cands.what: Article 334 ends the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha and State Assemblies 80 years after the Constitution began, on 25 January 2030.
cands.why: Parliament has extended the deadline every time, each shortly before it ran out: the 8th (1959), 23rd (1969), 45th (1980), 62nd (1989), 79th (1999), 95th (2009) and 104th (2019) Amendments. The last two passed both Houses within a week of being introduced.
cands.s: Extending reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Tribes

cands.t: How Lok Sabha seats are shared, and when seats reserved for women start
cands.stage: No Bill now. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026 on this subject was introduced on 16 April 2026 and did not get the two-thirds majority it needed in the Lok Sabha.
cands.what: Lok Sabha seats are shared among the States on the 1971 census, and constituencies follow the 2001 census, until figures from the first census taken after 2026 are published (Articles 81, 82 and 170). Census 2027 is expected to be that census. Seats reserved for women, a third of the total, start only after constituencies are redrawn on it (Article 334A).
cands.why: Parliament has changed this rule each time it came up: the 42nd Amendment (1976) set the freeze, the 84th (2001) extended it to 2026, and the 87th (2003) moved constituencies to the 2001 census. The Government's April 2026 Bill shows a change is being sought. Its defeat shows any change needs support across parties.

cands.tag: No Bill now; April 2026 Bill defeated

cands.t: Holding Lok Sabha and State Assembly elections together
cands.stage: Introduced in the Lok Sabha on 17 December 2024 and sent to a Joint Committee of both Houses. No report yet.
cands.what: Would add a new Article 82A and change Articles 83, 172 and 327 so that elections to the Lok Sabha and all State Assemblies are held at the same time.
cands.why: Recent Bills sent to a committee took about a year and a half to become law. Like the April 2026 Bill, it needs two-thirds of members present and voting in each House, so it needs support across parties. It lapses if the Lok Sabha is dissolved before it passes.
src: Lok Sabha synopsis, 20 December 2024 (sent to a Joint Committee)

cands.stage: Introduced in the Lok Sabha on 20 August 2025 and sent to a Joint Committee of both Houses. No report yet.
cands.what: Would require the removal of the Prime Minister, a Chief Minister or another Minister held in custody for 30 days in a row on a charge that can carry five years or more in prison. It changes Articles 75, 164 and 239AA.
cands.why: The same as above: a committee stage that has usually taken a long time, a two-thirds majority in each House, and lapse if the Lok Sabha is dissolved first.

cands.t: More powers for autonomous councils in the North East
cands.stage: Introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 6 February 2019. Not taken up since a parliamentary committee reported on it.
cands.what: Would give the autonomous councils in Assam, Meghalaya, Tripura and Mizoram more powers, and bring their funding into the Finance Commission's work (Article 280 and the Sixth Schedule).
cands.why: It has not moved for years. Bills introduced in the Rajya Sabha do not lapse when the Lok Sabha is dissolved, so it stays pending until it is passed, withdrawn or defeated.
cands.s: Autonomous councils in the North East

cands.t: A small family rule for MPs and MLAs
cands.stage: Introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 22 December 1992. Not taken up for over thirty years.
cands.what: Would make promoting a small family a duty of the State and of citizens, and disqualify MPs and MLAs who have more than two children.
cands.why: It has stayed pending in the Rajya Sabha since 1992 without being taken up.
cands.s: A small family rule for MPs and MLAs

cands.what: An amendment that has not been introduced at the time of writing.
cands.why: Half of the last 12 Amendment Acts passed both Houses within a week of being introduced, so the next one may not be on this list yet. Since 2006 the most common subject has been reservation, in 6 of 13 Acts.

clocks.s: Counting in most of India runs from 25 January to 5 March 2027. No date has been announced for publishing the figures.

clocks.t: The freeze on seat shares ends
clocks.s: Seats and constituencies are to be readjusted on the new census (Articles 81, 82 and 170). Seats reserved for women start after that redrawing (Article 334A).

clocks.t: This Lok Sabha's five-year term ends
clocks.s: It first sat on 24 June 2024 (Article 83). Bills still pending in the Lok Sabha lapse when it is dissolved (Article 107).

clocks.t: Reserved seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes end, unless extended
clocks.s: Set by Article 334, as last extended by the 104th Amendment (2019).

outcomes.note: Government Constitution Amendment Bills introduced since 2009, from Parliament's bill records. The two defeated were in 2011 and 2026.
